R001.text: Fix m, A and s as declared. Apply M001 to the Euclidean metric space R^m, its Borel measurable structure, exponent s and set A. At each finite positive scale, the formula's covers are exactly the covers in D002: a countable family can be enumerated by natural numbers, padding with empty sets if finite, and conversely a sequence is countable. All nonempty sets allowed at such a scale are bounded, so their extended diameters equal their ordinary finite Euclidean diameters. Empty members have cost zero in both definitions; since s>0, nonempty singletons also have zero cost. Thus the inner infimum is exactly the supplied scale content. The extra scale infinity in M001 adds nothing to the supremum: its admissible covers include all covers at scale 1, so its infimum is at most the scale-1 content. The finite positive extended scales are precisely the positive real scales. Taking their supremum proves F001: H^s(A)=μH[s](A). No dimensional normalization constant is introduced.

Use F001 to transport the four critical-exponent facts. Under L1: 0<s<dim_H(A), M002 with nonnegative exponent a=s gives μH[s](A)=infinity, hence H^s(A)=infinity; discharge L1. Under L2: dim_H(A)<s, M003 gives μH[s](A)=0, hence H^s(A)=0; discharge L2. Under L3: H^s(A)=0, F001 makes μH[s](A)=0≠infinity, and M004 gives dim_H(A)≤s; discharge L3. Under L4: H^s(A)=infinity, F001 and M005 give s≤dim_H(A); discharge L4. These are the complete conditional assertions F002.

The dimension in D004 is a supremum in the nonnegative extended reals, so it is nonnegative, including for the empty set. The arbitrary choices of m,A,s and F001-F002 prove every clause of the output proposition.

R002.text: By H003, E is compact, hence bounded in its Euclidean metric. A bounded subset of R^n is contained in a coordinate box [-b,b]^n for some b>0: each coordinate distance is at most the Euclidean distance, and increasing a bound if necessary makes it positive. This also holds in R^0. Record F001. H001 specifies the nonnegative ambient dimension; N001 gives D≥0.

Choose b from F001 and define C as declared. Under L1: n>0, fix arbitrary a and h under L2: a>n and L3: 0<h≤1. Divide each coordinate interval [-b,b] into ceil(2b/h) intervals of side at most h. Their number is at most (2b+1)/h in each coordinate, hence the resulting at most C h^(-n) closed cubes cover E. Each cube has Euclidean diameter at most sqrt(n)h. Therefore their total a-cost is at most C h^(-n)(sqrt(n)h)^a=C n^(a/2)h^(a-n). Since a-n>0, this tends to zero as h decreases to zero, and their diameters also tend to zero. In particular, at each fixed target scale arbitrarily small h provides admissible covers with costs tending to zero, so H^a(E)=0. Discharge L3 after using the arbitrary mesh sizes. N001 with A=E, exponent a gives D≤a. Since a>n was arbitrary, D≤n (if D>n, choose a strictly between n and D). Discharge L2 and L1. This proves F002.

Under L4: n=0, Euclidean R^0 consists of its single empty-coordinate point. H002 implies E=R^0. A cover by that singleton has diameter and s-cost zero for every positive exponent s. Thus H^s(E)=0 for all s>0, and N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, whence D=0 using D≥0. Discharge L4. By H001 the alternatives n=0 and n>0 exhaust the ambient dimensions. F002 and this branch give 0≤D≤n, so D is finite, with the stated singleton conclusion when n=0.

Fix arbitrary positive s and delta. The open balls of radius delta/2 centered at the points of E form an open cover. By H003 there is a finite subcover, and each such ball has diameter at most delta. Its finite number of members and finite diameters give a finite total s-cost. The defining infimum therefore gives H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this proves the output proposition.

R003.text: Fix arbitrary a under L1: a>1. For each positive integer N, divide I into N closed intervals of length 1/N. They have total a-cost N(1/N)^a=N^(1-a), which tends to zero as N tends to infinity, while their maximum diameter tends to zero. Thus at every positive target scale the defining infimum is zero, and H^a(I)=0. N001 applied with ambient dimension 1 gives dim_H(I)≤a; taking a down to 1 gives dim_H(I)≤1. Discharge L1 and record F001, including the universally quantified zero-measure assertion.

Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L2: V is a delta-cover of I. Define rho as declared; each rho_i≤delta is finite. Fix epsilon>0 and define J as declared. A nonempty V_i is bounded, so its real supremum and infimum exist and sup(V_i)-inf(V_i)=rho_i. Therefore V_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1), also when V_i is empty. The open sets J_i cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue measure and |I|=1 give 1≤sum_i |J_i|≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon, using sum_{i≥0}2^(-i-1)=1. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the required inequality is immediate; if finite, letting the arbitrary epsilon decrease to zero yields F002: sum_i rho_i≥1. All sets measured here are open intervals or I, so no measurability of V_i is assumed.

Fix arbitrary s under L3: 0<s<1. For each i with rho_i>0, rho_i≤delta and s-1<0 give rho_i^s=rho_i*rho_i^(s-1)≥delta^(s-1)*rho_i. The inequality also holds when rho_i=0 since s>0. Summing nonnegative terms and using F002 gives sum_i rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)sum_i rho_i≥delta^(s-1). Since V was an arbitrary delta-cover, taking the infimum gives H^s_delta(I)≥delta^(s-1). Discharge L2 in this universal cover conclusion. Since delta>0 was arbitrary and delta^(s-1) tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero, H^s(I)=infinity. N001 gives dim_H(I)≥s. Let s increase to 1 to get dim_H(I)≥1, and discharge L3. Together with F001 this is dim_H(I)=1 and all the measure assertions of the output proposition.

R004.text: Under L1: n=0, N002 gives E=R^0 and D=0. The coordinate map from I to F obtained by adjoining the unique R^0 coordinate preserves all distances. Fix arbitrary a under L4: a>1. N003 gives H^a(I)=0, so by the defining infimum there are covers of I at every positive scale with arbitrarily small a-cost. Push these covers forward by that coordinate map; their diameters are unchanged, so H^a(F)=0. N001 gives dim_H(F)≤a. Let the arbitrary a decrease to 1 to obtain dim_H(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L4 and L1 and record F000.

For the other branch introduce L2: n≥1. Fix arbitrary q under L3: q>D, and arbitrary positive delta and epsilon. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. Define r=min(1,delta/sqrt(2))>0; thus r≤1 and sqrt(2)r≤delta. By N001 applied to E, H^q(E)=0. The nonnegative content H^q_r(E) is at most this supremum, hence zero. The infimum defining that content therefore supplies a countable r-cover W with total q-cost<epsilon/2. The infimum is zero, so its admissible family is nonempty (an empty infimum is infinity); its defining approximation property gives the stated cover. This is the existence statement F001, before choosing W.

Choose W from F001. Define beta,U,K,r_i as declared. A nonempty zero-diameter Euclidean set is a singleton. Because n≥1, its replacement open ball has positive diameter beta_i≤r and q-cost beta_i^q≤epsilon*2^(-i-3)<epsilon*2^(-i-2). Nonempty positive-diameter members are unchanged; every point originally covered remains covered. The additional cost is at most sum_{i≥0}epsilon*2^(-i-3)=epsilon/4<epsilon/2. Thus, after discarding empty members by restricting to K, U is a countable cover of E with 0<r_i≤r and sum_{i∈K}r_i^q<epsilon. This is F002; the countable index set may be finite.

For i∈K define N_i=ceil(1/r_i). Divide I into N_i closed intervals, each of length 1/N_i≤r_i. Since r_i≤1, N_i≤1/r_i+1≤2/r_i. The products of U_i with these intervals form a countable cover of F. The Euclidean distance formula in D006 shows that every product member has diameter at most sqrt(2)r_i≤sqrt(2)r≤delta. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
sum_(i∈K) N_i (sqrt(2)r_i)^(q+1)
≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1) sum_(i∈K) r_i^q
<2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon.
These inequalities follow termwise from N_i≤2/r_i and then by nonnegative summation, so they remain valid for countably many members. Consequently H^(q+1)_delta(F)≤2(sqrt(2))^(q+1)epsilon, which is F003.

For fixed q and delta, epsilon>0 was arbitrary; the content in F003 is independent of epsilon, so it is zero. Since delta>0 was arbitrary, H^(q+1)(F)=0. N001, with ambient dimension n+1 and positive exponent q+1, gives dim_H(F)≤q+1. Since q>D was arbitrary and D is finite by N002, let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1: an alleged strict excess would allow a q between D and dim_H(F)-1, contradicting this bound (an infinite dimension is already excluded by any one q>D). Discharge L3 and L2. This proves F004.
A natural dimension n is either zero or at least one. F000 and F004 thus give dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. By N002 the right hand side is finite, proving the finiteness clause as well.

R005.text: Fix s>0, delta>0 and an arbitrary sequence V under L1: V covers F and diam(V_i)≤delta for all i. Empty members may be discarded; equivalently retain them with all ensuing projections and intervals empty and costs zero. Define rho,A_i,B_i and c as declared. Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz for the Euclidean metric in D006: each squared coordinate distance is bounded by the sum of the squared horizontal and vertical distances. Hence diam(A_i),diam(B_i)≤rho_i≤delta. In particular a nonempty B_i is a nonempty bounded subset of R. N002 applies to the positive s,delta and gives c<infinity.

Fix arbitrary epsilon>0 and set eta_i=epsilon*2^(-i-1)/(1+rho_i^s)>0. Define J as declared. For a nonempty B_i, its supremum minus its infimum equals its diameter and is at most rho_i by F001. Thus B_i⊆J_i and |J_i|≤rho_i+eta_i. The empty-member convention makes both assertions true for empty V_i as well. The J_i are open measurable sets and enclose the possibly nonmeasurable projections. This construction needs no measurability of V_i,A_i or B_i.

Define the nonnegative functions f_i(t)=rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t). They are measurable because each J_i is open and each coefficient is a fixed finite nonnegative real. Under L2: t∈I, for every x∈E the point (x,t) lies in F, so some V_i contains it. Then x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Thus the family of A_i with t∈J_i is a delta-cover of E, and the defining infimum and diam(A_i)≤rho_i give c≤sum_i rho_i^s indicator_(J_i)(t)=sum_i f_i(t). The point x here is universally bound in this coverage argument, and i is its existential cover index. Discharge L2 into the assertion for every t∈I. Record F003.

Set μ=λ|I. It is a measure on the Borel real line with μ(R)=λ(I)=1. Apply M006 with α=R, its Borel structure, index type β=N, this measure μ and the functions f of F003. Borel measurability implies μ-almost-everywhere measurability for each summand. Monotonicity of the nonnegative integral and the integral of a constant on a set of measure one give
c≤∫_I sum_i f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i ∫_I f_i(t) dλ
 =sum_i rho_i^s |J_i∩I|
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+sum_i eta_i rho_i^s
 ≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon.
Here the middle equality is the integral of a measurable indicator times its nonnegative coefficient. The first inequality inside the sum uses F002 and distributivity of nonnegative sums. Finally eta_i rho_i^s=epsilon*2^(-i-1)*rho_i^s/(1+rho_i^s)≤epsilon*2^(-i-1), whose sum is epsilon. All sums and integrals are nonnegative and may be infinite; c is finite by F001. This is F004.

If sum_i rho_i^(s+1)=infinity, c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1) holds immediately. Otherwise F004 holds for every epsilon>0 with c and V fixed, so letting epsilon decrease to zero gives the same inequality c≤sum_i rho_i^(s+1). The cover V was arbitrary under L1. Take the infimum over all its possible delta-covers of F and discharge L1, obtaining H^s_delta(E)≤H^(s+1)_delta(F). Since s>0 and delta>0 were arbitrary, this is precisely the output proposition.

R006.text: Temporarily assume L1: D>0 and L2: 0<s<D for arbitrary real s. N001 gives H^s(E)=infinity. Fix any T>0. By the definition of H^s as the supremum of the scale contents, there exists a positive delta with H^s_delta(E)>T; otherwise their supremum would be at most the finite T. Moreover these contents are nondecreasing as scale decreases, since a cover admissible at a smaller scale is admissible at any larger one. Thus any such bound remains valid on decreasing its scale, so the contents become arbitrarily large at arbitrarily small scales. Record the existence F001 before making a choice.

Choose delta from F001. N005 applies to the positive s and delta and gives H^(s+1)_delta(F)≥H^s_delta(E)>T. Taking the supremum defining H^(s+1)(F) yields H^(s+1)(F)>T. This is F002, independent of the chosen scale.
Since F002 holds for the arbitrary positive finite T, H^(s+1)(F)=infinity. N001 applies with ambient dimension n+1 and exponent s+1>0, giving dim_H(F)≥s+1. Record F003.

By N002, D is finite; under L1 it is positive. F003 holds for every s with 0<s<D. Such s can increase to D, so their s+1 have supremum D+1 and dim_H(F)≥D+1. Equivalently every real number below D+1 is below some s+1 with 0<s<D. Discharge L2 in this universal limiting argument and then L1, obtaining the complete conditional output.

R007.text: Temporarily assume L1: D=0. By H002 choose x_0∈E and define f(t)=(x_0,t). The Euclidean metric formula in D006 gives dist(f(t),f(u))=|t-u| for all real t,u, including n=0. Thus f restricts to an isometric embedding of I into F.

Fix arbitrary s under L2: 0<s<1. For any delta>0 and arbitrary V under L3: V is a delta-cover of F, define W as declared. F001 shows W covers I, and isometry gives diam(W_i)≤diam(V_i)≤delta. Hence H^s_delta(I)≤sum_i diam(V_i)^s. Take the infimum over V, discharge L3, and then take the supremum over positive delta to get H^s(I)≤H^s(F). This proves the particular dimension-monotonicity implication used here directly from covers. N003 gives H^s(I)=infinity, so H^s(F)=infinity. N001 applied to F and exponent s yields dim_H(F)≥s.

Since F002 holds for every s with 0<s<1, letting s increase to 1 gives dim_H(F)≥1. Discharge L2. Under L1, 1=D+1, so this proves the asserted bound. Discharge L1 to obtain the output proposition. The argument used only the isometric embedding from a point of E, and applies unchanged to the singleton ambient space R^0.

R008.text: N002 gives finite D≥0. Thus either D>0 or D=0. In the positive case N006 gives dim_H(F)≥D+1; in the zero case N007 gives the identical bound, including n=0. N004 supplies dim_H(F)≤D+1 in all cases. Antisymmetry gives dim_H(F)=D+1. Substituting F=E×[0,1] and D=dim_H(E), with the Euclidean identification of D006, proves the complete target P.

187: proofs are never an input source for these stages.
188: 
189: The Yui arm receives only the declared Yui rules and task material. The direct
190: arm receives a minimal task/tool contract and the same mathematical inputs,
191: without Yui planning, strategy or shared-proof guidance. Log controller-supplied instructions, frozen inputs, native configuration,
192: tool schemas/results, reported model identity, phase, usage and health. Native
193: Codex manages model networking and context; Yui does not intercept HTTP payloads.
194: Actual tier and per-response usage coverage remain unknown when not exposed. Never execute model-generated Python or shell text.
195: 
196: Collect the active phase profiles as described above. `config.json` supplies
197: defaults only when explicitly selected. The current isolated native Codex carrier requests
198: Standard speed and checks model/effort availability without fallback. Freeze
199: and record each stage's selected profile;
200: never silently substitute a stronger model or fallback.

1: # Minimal translation from accepted NL0
2: 
3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 300-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

1: # Shared-lemma extraction as a local NL0 revision
2: 
3: ## Scope and position
4: 
5: Apply this procedure at the start of **NL0-to-Lean translation**, before final
6: interface/planning freeze or worker-packet generation. It is not an extra
7: requirement for a task that requests NL0 alone. The input is an existing,
8: versioned NL0, not an invitation to reconstruct its proof.
9: 
10: The operation is proof factoring: move an already supplied local derivation
11: into one shared N/R pair and replace its occurrences by explicit applications.
12: Do not rewrite the whole NL0, regenerate its prose, reprove unchanged results,
13: or seek a stronger/general theorem for speculative future reuse. Reading the
14: existing graph to locate candidates is not a new proof-construction task.
15: If an existing N already exports the needed fact, reuse that node directly.
16: 
17: Use [the revision record](../templates/source-refactoring.md). Preserve the
18: original package and audit as immutable evidence. Write a revised package in
19: a new directory; retain existing IDs and keep the revision identity in the
20: sidecar record. Generated Markdown/diagrams are views, never patch authorities.
21: 
22: ## 1. Locate and qualify candidates without reconstructing NL0
23: 
24: Start with existing node statements, direct inputs, definitions and any
25: available index. Locate repeated subarguments using their mathematical role,
26: objects, formulas or operation names; then inspect the actual candidate spans
27: and the local context they need. Do not commission a new proof or a full prose
28: summary for every node as a discovery method. Text similarity is only a lead.
29: 
30: For each proposed lemma record:
31: 
32: - The complete mathematical statement, all parameters/conditions and proposed
33:   direct input IDs, together with exact old graph pointers or paragraph spans.
34: - The existing derivation to reuse and every occurrence that will consume it.
35:   The derivation must actually supply the proposed statement; a summary label
36:   or a theorem believed true from memory is insufficient.
37: - Identify the baseline revision/old paragraph IDs separately from the current
38:   new producer. A new N's origin label must state the historical/current
39:   distinction; a bare old R number is ambiguous after consumer editing.
40: - The expected avoided repeated work. An occurrence count is not measured
41:   formalization cost and does not by itself establish a speed benefit.
42: - The scope at each occurrence, including bound variables, temporary
43:   assumptions, definition guards and local facts established before the span.
44: 
45: Prefer a statement already justified at the cuts. Do not generalize its domain,
46: change representations, weaken conditions or introduce new mathematics merely
47: to make more occurrences match. If the proposed derivation needs an earlier
48: local calculation, include that calculation with its justified inputs. Never
49: declare an unexported local fact to be an available graph input.
50: 
51: Temporary assumptions stay closed in an implication or other complete
52: proposition; they cannot become H roots. An extraction that moves a witness,
53: choice, definition or binder across a scope boundary needs an explicit account
54: of the values and properties used afterwards. If that account cannot be made
55: locally and clearly, leave the original argument in place.
56: 
57: ## 2. Write the patch boundary before editing
58: 
59: Prepare an edit allowlist for one candidate or one coherent batch:
60: 
61: | Part | Allowed edit |
62: | --- | --- |
63: | New shared theorem | One fresh N and its R producer, with a complete statement and derivation from existing permitted inputs. |
64: | Actual consumers | Replace only the located repeated proof spans by a complete application; adjust direct inputs, citations and application accounting accordingly. |
65: | Necessary local bookkeeping | Update the directly affected binder/reference accounting and generated views. Record every such edit explicitly. |
66: | Everything else | Preserve the existing record content; do not reorder or renumber it as a cleanup. |
67: 
68: Keep the entire frozen specification unchanged: target P, original H, parameter
69: domains, global definitions/notation, logic, pins and E/M source inventories and
70: statements. Preserve all existing N/P statements and every unmodified argument
71: span. New sources, changed hypotheses, new global definitions, removed existing
72: nodes, or a changed old output are outside this fast factoring operation.
73: 
74: Copy an existing derivation rather than writing a new proof route. The new
75: producer may use only its declared inputs, global definitions and legitimate
76: local derivations. It cannot depend on a consumer output or its descendants.
77: Do not split each consumer into additional source nodes around the shared fact.
78: 
79: Each consumer application must state the parameter substitution, which inputs
80: or local proved facts discharge each condition, and the exact conclusion used.
81: Remove a former direct input only if the remaining argument no longer uses it;
82: retain it when it still has a direct role. A shared theorem is never ambient.
83: 
84: If an edit escapes the allowlist, return that candidate to the shortlist or
85: leave it unextracted. A source defect goes through the existing gap procedure;
86: do not turn a reuse optimization into a repair or a new research route.
87: 
88: ## 3. Check structural preservation globally, reasoning locally
89: 
90: Compare canonical JSON records by stable IDs, not only rendered text or changed
91: line numbers. Record before/after hashes and the actual changed fields/spans.
92: Reject any unexplained diff. Check these global mechanical invariants:
93: 
94: - The frozen specification and protected records are unchanged.
95: - All IDs/references resolve; definitions and guards remain available; there
96:   is no cycle or unsupported initial node; every N/P still has one producer.
97: - Every retained node remains in P's dependency closure. Reject the candidate
98:   if it would require deleting or reorganizing unrelated nodes to restore this.
99: - All consumers declare their actual inputs and remain self-contained. Only
100:   the explicit allowlisted nodes/fields have changed.
101: 
102: Run the existing `../scripts/nl0.py check` on the revised graph and specification.
103: Rechecking graph metadata across the package is allowed and inexpensive relative
104: to rereading every mathematical proof. It does not require a new LLM proof of
105: every node, and it does not establish the semantics of a substitution.
106: 
107: Distinguish **review impact** from **dependency status**. The new producer and
108: edited application boundaries need new mathematical review. An unchanged
109: downstream proof whose input statements and conventions are unchanged need not
110: be reconstructed merely because its ancestors have a new producer. Its final
111: acceptance nevertheless depends on the replacement producer being accepted.
112: Until that happens, affected descendants are pending, not newly accepted.
113: 
114: ## 4. Incremental Audit A: review the new proof and the substitution cuts
115: 
116: This is an incremental review procedure under Audit A's mathematical
117: obligations, not permission to weaken source verification or invent a fresh
118: packet replay. The version-bound receipt limitation below is part of the rule.
119: 
120: First inspect the baseline audit and its evidence bindings. Reuse a judgment
121: only for the exact previously reviewed content, context and evidence. Carry
122: FAIL, UNVERIFIED, inaccessible sources and disclosure limits forward. A source
123: file hash proves byte identity, not that an auditor ever inspected the theorem.
124: An unaudited baseline cannot acquire whole-proof acceptance through extraction.
125: 
126: Review the **new N/R in full**: complete statement, exact inputs, argument,
127: dependency accounting, scopes, guards and E/M applications, and the normal
128: fresh packet-only replay requirement. The extracted proof may be copied, but
129: its new closed interface and context must actually be checked.
130: 
131: For **each changed consumer**, review a substitution cut rather than rewriting
132: or replaying its entire old proof by default:
133: 
134: 1. Compare the old derived conclusion at the cut with the instantiated shared
135:    result, including all conditions, quantifiers and semantic conventions.
136: 2. Check that every condition of the shared theorem follows from that consumer's
137:    declared inputs or explicit in-scope local derivations, without extra facts.
138: 3. Check the interface to the untouched continuation: every subsequently used
139:    proposition, object, value and scope remains available with the same meaning.
140:    Equal output text alone cannot establish preservation of a selected witness.
141: 4. Verify the changed direct-input/citation/application accounting. Reuse source
142:    identity evidence only when unchanged; check every new source application.
143: 5. Bind the untouched remainder to its old reviewed bytes and old review
144:    evidence. Record exactly which old checks are inherited and which new checks
145:    cover the patch. Do not relabel this comparison as a new fresh whole-R replay.
146: 
147: If those boundaries do not justify inheritance, mark that candidate
148: `DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL` and keep the baseline argument. Do not automatically expand
149: to a full-case audit. A separately requested broader review may inspect the
150: specific unresolved node, but is not part of this fast extraction.
151: 
152: Unchanged target/source/definition reviews and proof regions need no new
153: mathematical re-review when their audited content, applicable context and
154: evidence are unchanged. Do not reopen source searches solely because a global
155: graph hash changed. Changes or failures in their evidence invalidate reuse.
156: 
157: The result is a chain: baseline audit + exact revision + actual new reviews.
158: It is not a copied PASS with an updated graph hash. Record actual reviewer
159: exposure; old-review access is appropriate for delta review and cannot be called
160: an independent fresh packet-only review. This procedure authorizes no additional
161: agent or external-service dispatch.
162: 
163: ## 5. Seal or leave the candidate unextracted
164: 
165: Seal only after the allowlist/diff and graph checks pass and the scoped
166: mathematical review is complete. Keep original and revised manifests, patch,
167: location map, old/new evidence, pending findings and measured preparation cost.
168: Stage all candidate edits transactionally; a failed candidate must not replace
169: the accepted baseline. Do not launch formalization workers for an unaccepted
170: source revision or reuse task packets bound to the old graph.
171: 
172: Then finalize and freeze typed interfaces, shared Lean ports and local plans;
173: only afterwards generate worker packets. Shared Lean interface discovery may
174: use this preparation pass, but must not silently mutate the sealed NL0 later.
175: No extraction is a valid outcome; do not manufacture shared lemmas to satisfy
176: the workflow. The work is bounded by the chosen proof regions and patch size,
177: not a universal minute count. Longer time alone is not a mathematical gap.
178: 
179: ## Executable acceptance and review responsibilities
180: 
181: The unchanged parent checker still binds ordinary format-4 audit to the complete
182: graph. `scripts/source_preparation.py` adds a separate incremental record;
183: it never copies old PASS fields into a forged fresh whole-graph audit.
184: Audit B and `workflow.py` both revalidate that record and all underlying evidence.
185: See [commands and the patch contract](integrated-workflow.md).
186: 
187: The initial executable scope is current-v2 source and nonoverlapping consumer
188: paragraph substitutions. Old proposition records/specification, unlisted R
189: records, untouched paragraphs and local fact/assumption lifetimes are protected.
190: Consumer source-application changes can remove obsolete uses, not introduce new
191: external uses. A broader refactor is deferred rather than widening this operation.
192: Multiple proposed edits to one consumer must first be merged into one coherent
193: candidate or left unextracted. Legacy test copies remain development evidence.
194: 
195: Separate three responsibilities:
196: 
197: - A producer reviewer sees only the complete new per-R packet and audits its
198:   conditional mathematics under ordinary Audit A, including actual fresh replay.
199:   Do not ask that packet to establish whole-graph acceptance or old-copy provenance.
200: - A substitution reviewer sees paired before/after consumers, the proposed shared
201:   statement, original derivations and explicit cut contract. `old_derivation`
202:   names THIS consumer's replaced proof; `producer_source_derivation` names the
203:   one original proof used to export the shared lemma. Its supplier may be a
204:   different consumer with a different final goal. Compare the common intermediate
205:   conclusion, not equality of those final goals. Check existing-proof
206:   factoring, each condition, exact supplied conclusion, continuation and accounting.
207:   This is delta review with baseline access, not fresh whole-consumer replay.
208: - Python checks canonical fanout, edit scope, graph validity, immutable evidence,
209:   the exact coverage partition and inherited acceptance/qualifications. It does
210:   not judge natural-language mathematics or authenticate a dishonest reviewer.
211: 
212: Internal N applications are direct inputs, paragraph citations and explicit prose;
213: the parent's `applications` source records remain E/M-only. Do not invent an N
214: source-application record to satisfy a reviewer. A prose citation without a real
215: substitution is not successful factoring. Derivation labels and fanout guesses
216: from a model are leads, not canonical graph facts.
217: 
218: Each cut review binds the exact supplied packet hash. Retain the binding from
219: the generated template and verify it during acceptance. Reusing an actual old
220: review after a record-only change requires identical canonical mathematics and
221: byte-identical actual reviewed packets; preserve its verdicts, notes, evidence
222: and original cost, and disclose that no new mathematical review occurred.
223: 
224: `INCREMENTAL-AUDIT-A-PASSED` requires a passing current baseline plus all actual
225: new producer/cut reviews. Missing/failed baseline checks remain inherited and
226: yield development-only local review. Every later consumer acceptance still
227: depends on the new producer; unchanged input statements and context permit
228: inheriting the old conditional argument without rereading it mathematically.
229: No fixed completion-time threshold makes a candidate worthwhile or incorrect.

# Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H(E)+1, with R^n×R identified with Euclidean R^(n+1), including n=0.

parameters.type: natural number (encoding the original nonnegative integer)

hypotheses.origin: problem.md:21; the original nonnegative integer is represented by a natural number.
problem.md:16-22; explicitly approved addition to the printed exercise.

hypotheses.statement: E is compact in Euclidean R^n.

definitions.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric or extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a subset A of a metric or extended metric space X, diam(A)=sup{dist(x,y):x,y in A}, using extended distance and sup(empty)=0. For bounded subsets of a Euclidean space it is identified with its finite nonnegative real value; diam(empty)=0.

definitions.type: scale contents H^s_delta(A) and unnormalized Hausdorff measure H^s(A), valued in [0,infinity]
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension.

definitions.type: library Hausdorff measure, a measure on a Borel extended metric space for each real exponent
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space X with its Borel measurable structure and real a, μH[a] denotes the native MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a, defined as mkMetric(r↦r^a). Here mkMetric is the Borel measure associated to the metric outer measure obtained by taking the supremum over positive diameter scales of the outer measures generated by costs on sets of diameter at most that scale. Empty sets have zero cost. This uses the native extended-real-power convention at a=0. Values on arbitrary subsets are outer-measure values. Its explicit countable-cover formula is invoked as a source theorem in the proof.

binders.type: extended metric space with Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an extended metric space, valued in [0,infinity]
definitions.definition: dim_H(A) is the native Hausdorff dimension dimH A: with the Borel structure it is sup{a : a is a nonnegative real and μH[a](A)=infinity}, where the supremum is taken in [0,infinity] and sup(empty)=0. Thus dim_H(empty)=0. This is the usual Hausdorff dimension. The proof identifies μH with the supplied unnormalized measure H on Euclidean spaces at every positive exponent; the zero exponent can contribute only the value zero to this supremum.
I=[0,1], with the usual Euclidean distance.

F=E×I. The coordinate identification (x,t)↦(x_1,...,x_n,t) identifies R^n×R with R^(n+1); throughout this product has Euclidean distance sqrt(||x-y||_2^2+|t-u|^2). In particular R^0 is the one-point Euclidean space and this formula also applies when n=0.
D=dim_H(E), initially an extended nonnegative real. Its finiteness is proved before any use of its real value; after that proof it is identified with the corresponding finite nonnegative real.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line
definitions.definition: λ is Lebesgue measure on R. Write |J|=λ(J), λ|I for its restriction to I, and ∫_I g dλ for the nonnegative (extended-valued) Lebesgue integral with respect to λ|I. Intervals have their usual Lebesgue lengths.

definitions.type: indicator function with values zero and one
definitions.definition: indicator_J(t)=1 when t∈J and 0 otherwise. This notation is used also as 1_J(t), with nonnegative real or extended nonnegative real values as appropriate.

4: [executable guide](../references/integrated-workflow.md). This worksheet is not

8: 
9: ## Baseline and scope

12: - Baseline Audit A path/SHA256, exact scope, actual status and reviewer disclosure:

54: - Inputs, argument, accounting and exact output: UNVERIFIED

value.statement: For every natural m, subset A⊆R^m and positive real s, H^s(A)=μH[s](A). Consequently: if s>dim_H(A) then H^s(A)=0; if 0<s<dim_H(A) then H^s(A)=infinity; H^s(A)=0 implies dim_H(A)≤s; H^s(A)=infinity implies dim_H(A)≥s. Dimension is nonnegative, including for the empty set.
